# Awesome TLS / burp-awesome-tls-plus

> Burp Suite extension that spoofs browser TLS fingerprints (JA3/JA4/ClientHello). Repository name: **burp-awesome-tls-plus**. Fork of sleeyax/burp-awesome-tls with per-domain rules and full-tool coverage.

## Project identity

- Product name: Awesome TLS
- **GitHub repository (this project):** https://github.com/Robin528919/burp-awesome-tls-plus
- Upstream (original): https://github.com/sleeyax/burp-awesome-tls
- Latest release (as of 2026-08-07): v2.3.1 — https://github.com/Robin528919/burp-awesome-tls-plus/releases
- License: GPL-3.0
- Languages: Java (Burp UI + HttpHandler), Go (local TLS spoof server via JNA c-shared)
- Platforms: **8** prebuilt OS/arch targets (macOS x64/arm64, Linux x86/x64/arm/arm64, Windows x86/x64) + fat jar
- Burp: Professional and Community

## One-sentence definition

**burp-awesome-tls-plus** hijacks Burp’s outbound HTTP/TLS path and re-sends each eligible request through a local Go server (utls / tls-client) so destinations observe a chosen browser TLS fingerprint instead of Java’s default stack.

## Facts (citable)

- Named fingerprint profiles in the UI list: **80** (`default` + 79 keys from bogdanfinn/tls-client `profiles.MappedTLSClients`)
- Burp tools with spoofed fingerprint: **all of them** — Proxy, Repeater, Intruder, Scanner, plus requests other extensions send
- Suite-internal Burp traffic (e.g. updates, Collaborator polling) is the one exception: not redirected
- Domain rules: exact host or `*.suffix`; most-specific match wins; empty cells inherit Defaults
- Rules file lives outside the Burp project, in an OS config dir named `burp-awesome-tls-plus/` (same name as the repository; a pre-rename `burp-awesome-tls/` directory is migrated on first start)

## Who it is for

- Penetration testers and security researchers using Burp Suite
- Users blocked by Cloudflare, Akamai, DataDome, PerimeterX, or similar TLS fingerprinting
- Teams needing different fingerprints per target domain and shareable rule JSON

## What this fork adds vs upstream

- Per-domain fingerprint rules (exact / wildcard) with global defaults as fallback
- Spoofing for every Burp tool, not Proxy-only
- Auto-save + import/export of rules.json
- Hand-written Swing UI with Burp theme support; several upstream save/forward bugs fixed
- Full matrix: https://github.com/Robin528919/burp-awesome-tls-plus/blob/main/docs/comparison.md

## Architecture (short)

1. Burp HttpHandler rewrites eligible requests: magic header `Awesometlsconfig`, service redirected to local spoof server.
2. Local HTTPS Go server parses config, strips header, builds utls/tls-client with selected fingerprint, forwards to real destination.
3. Response streams back to Burp. Re-entry avoided via magic header; suite tools skipped.

## Constraints

- Hex ClientHello wins over named Fingerprint when both are set for a scope.
- Advanced intercept capture is global and overrides domain rules once a fingerprint is captured.
- New tls-client instance per request (no cross-request connection pool).
- Authorized testing only; not a full bypass of JS challenges or IP reputation.
